lessons.title: Soil, water and veld as farm capital
lessons.html:
Soil, water and veld as farm capital

Natural resources are the farm's long-term capital. A farm that mines its soil, water and veld may profit for a few seasons and then decline. Good management keeps the resources productive for the next generation.

Soil

  • Erosion by water and wind removes the most fertile topsoil. Signs: sheet wash, rills, dongas, dust storms off bare lands.
  • Controls: contour cultivation, contour banks and waterways, conservation agriculture (minimum tillage, permanent soil cover, crop rotation), windbreaks, keeping cover on lands after harvest.
  • Fertility: regular soil sampling and analysis, liming acid soils, balanced fertilisation, organic matter from residues and manure.
  • Compaction from heavy machinery and trampling reduces root growth and infiltration.

Water

Water is South Africa's most limiting resource. The National Water Act 36 of 1998 states that water is a national resource; irrigation and storage beyond certain limits require authorisation, and users must protect water resources from pollution.

  • Measure and record water use from boreholes, dams and irrigation.
  • Use efficient irrigation scheduled by soil moisture or crop need.
  • Protect wetlands and riparian zones; keep livestock and chemicals away from streams.
  • Harvest rainwater and maintain dams and pipelines to cut losses.

Veld

  • Veld condition is assessed by species composition, basal cover and productivity.
  • Overgrazing leads to loss of palatable grasses, bush encroachment and erosion.
  • Rotational grazing with rest periods, correct stocking rates and controlled burning where appropriate maintain veld.
  • CARA (Act 43 of 1983) regulates the protection of vegetation, control of weeds and invader plants, and the use of veld.

lessons.title: Managing infrastructure, energy, labour and finance
lessons.html:
Managing infrastructure, energy, labour and finance

Infrastructure and machinery

  • Keep an asset register: tractors, implements, bakkies, pumps, handling facilities, fences, buildings.
  • Schedule preventive maintenance by hours or season: services, greasing, tyre and battery checks.
  • Calculate cost per hour of machinery to decide between owning, hiring or using contractors.
  • Maintain fences, water points and handling facilities (crush, kraal, loading ramp) for safe and efficient livestock work.

Energy

Diesel and electricity are major costs. Irrigation pumping and cold storage are heavy electricity users, and supply interruptions disrupt operations. Options include scheduling pumping in off-peak periods, solar pumping for boreholes, solar systems with storage, efficient motors and good tractor management (correct tyre pressure, matched implements, reduced tillage passes).

Labour

  • Plan labour around the farm calendar: planting, harvest, lambing, shearing.
  • Comply with labour legislation, including the sectoral determination for farm workers and the Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997.
  • Invest in skills; trained workers handle animals, machines and chemicals more safely and productively.
  • Provide a safe workplace as required by the OHS Act 85 of 1993.

Finance as a resource

  • Prepare annual budgets and monthly cash flows; seasonal income from harvest or auction must cover year-round costs.
  • Use production credit carefully; match loan terms to the life of the asset.
  • Insure against key risks: hail, fire, theft, livestock losses.

Monitoring

Use simple indicators each season: soil analysis trends, veld condition photos at fixed points, water use per hectare or per tonne, machinery cost per hectare, and gross margins. These show whether resources are improving or declining.

Key points

  • Soil, water and veld are the farm's long-term capital.
  • Control erosion with cover, contours and conservation agriculture.
  • The National Water Act 36 of 1998 governs water use and protection.
  • Maintain assets, manage energy and plan labour around the calendar.
  • Budget, plan cash flow and monitor resource indicators every season.
